definition: Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate, plus Complete, Consistent, Enduring, Available. Data-integrity principles applied by FDA/MHRA to GxP records. In HOS the ledger is the "original" record (`docs/10`).
the region of input space where a predictive model is reliable. Every `PREDICTED` quantity carries an `ApplicabilityCheck`; out-of-domain predictions are flagged.
a human electronic signature with legal meaning. Only human principals holding the role can sign (`hos/kernel/attestation.py`).
intrinsic clearance. `CLint,app` (µL/min/mg microsomal protein) is the in vitro value; `CLint,in vivo` (mL/min/kg) is scaled to the whole liver.
hepatic blood clearance, here from the well-stirred model.
the shared test battery every study driver must pass (`docs/08`).
contract research organisation; an external laboratory that executes a study.
Common Technical Document (ICH M4); Module 4 holds the nonclinical study reports, numbered 4.2.1 (pharmacology), 4.2.2 (pharmacokinetics), 4.2.3 (toxicology).
a package implementing `StudyDriver` for one study type: design, plan, data template, instruction package, ingest, analysis, interpretation, report and optional simulation.
multiple comparison of several treatment groups against one control (Dunnett 1955).
where a study's work physically runs: an external laboratory, an in-house laboratory, or a simulation.
CLh / Qh; the fraction of drug removed in one pass through the liver.
unbound fraction of drug in the microsomal incubation.
unbound fraction in blood / plasma.
Good Laboratory Practice, 21 CFR Part 58 (US) / OECD Principles of GLP.
the regulated and non-regulated halves of the system (`docs/10`).
human equivalent dose, from an animal NOAEL by body-surface-area scaling (FDA 2005).
the potassium channel (KCNH2) carrying the rapid delayed rectifier current; inhibition can delay ventricular repolarisation (QT prolongation).
Investigational New Drug application (21 CFR 312).
in vitro–in vivo extrapolation.
body weight ÷ body surface area for a species (FDA 2005 Table 1).
the append-only hash-chained record of every state change (`hos/kernel/ledger.py`).
minimal anticipated biological effect level (EMA FIH guideline).
microsomal protein per gram liver (mg/g).
maximum recommended starting dose for first-in-human trials (FDA 2005).
no-observed-adverse-effect level. In HOS a NOAEL is a **human determination** recorded with a Study Director signature; the system reports statistics but never decides it.
pharmacologically active dose.
one of measured, literature, computed, predicted, guideline, user-supplied, simulated, unavailable (`docs/07` §7.2).
hepatic blood flow (mL/min/kg).
the provenance-typed value object; the only form in which a scientific number exists.
CDISC Standard for Exchange of Nonclinical Data.
data generated by a declared, cited model with recorded parameters and seed. Used for software verification and demonstration; never admissible as evidence.
the list of nonclinical studies a programme needs, derived from ICH rules and the programme context (`hos/core/regulatory`).
the individual with overall responsibility for a GLP study (21 CFR 58.33).
the honest representation of a missing value: no number, a stated reason.
women of childbearing potential.
